question.value: Is the fragmentation of a massive, dense, turbulent clump regulated by magnetic support? ALMA fragment populations are compared with 3D RMHD simulations with strong (mu=2) and weak (mu=200) magnetization.

evidence.quote: we demonstrate that the fragmentation due to self-gravity is dominated by the magnetic support
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA.2012.1.00366.S.
dust thermal continuum emission at $\sim 278$ GHz
In this letter, we only use the N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ (3–2) line to derive the virial masses
The total bandwidth used is $\sim 1703$ MHz.
The array was in configuration C36-6, with maximum baseline of 1091 m.
The angular resolution of the final image is $\sim 0.25$ $^{\prime\prime}$ (i.e.$\sim 900$ AU at the source distance).
We were sensitive to point-like fragments of 0.06 M$_\odot$.
The total integration time on source was $\sim 18$ minutes.
Observations of I16061c1 with the ALMA array were performed during southern winter, 2015.

findings_qualitative.value: ALMA continuum shows a filamentary east-west chain of condensations, matching mu=2 morphology; mu=200 is chaotic and never filamentary

claims.hypothesis: Fragmentation of I16061c1 is regulated by magnetic support
claims.experiment: Compare ALMA fragment population with RMHD synthetic ALMA images for mu=2 and mu=200
claims.result: mu=200 excluded at >99.8% by Anderson-Darling; mu=2 not excluded in the (y,z) projection; mu=2 is filamentary like the data
claims.finding: Strong magnetic support (mu=2) best reproduces the data

evidence.quote: undoubtedly the model that better reproduces the data is the one with $\mu$=2.

claims.experiment: Virial masses from N2H+ line widths versus continuum masses
claims.result: Mvir/M ~0.4 without magnetic support; ~1 with 0.27 mG
claims.finding: Gravity appears to dominate but the fragments are marginally stable if magnetic support is included; inconclusive

evidence.quote: it is difficult to conclude that the fragments are unstable.
